A barrel is where fermentation happens. You pour the must into the bucket, put whatever the recipe asks for into the slots, and when the clock runs out the drink comes down into the tap. <LINE> <LINE> Pick a recipe from the dropdown first. The card then lists everything that recipe wants, line by line; hover a line to see which recipe that ingredient comes from and what else the barrel takes in its place. If you already carry the goods, Prepare is all you need - it fetches the missing pieces out of your inventory by itself. When the button stays dim, the line under it tells you what is short. <LINE> <LINE> You can load the slots by hand as well. Left click empties a full slot and opens the add menu on an empty one; right click always brings up the menu. <LINE> <LINE> A finished batch flows into the tap and waits there. Nothing new can finish until you draw it into a container, so empty the tap before you walk away. <LINE> <LINE> The second tab holds the upgrades. A fitted part either shortens the brewing time or raises the yield, and its tooltip says which jobs it touches. The three slots open at Brewing 3, 6 and 9. <LINE> <LINE> The strip at the top shows the temperature. A barrel that drifts out of its range stops counting, but nothing is spoiled - it picks up where it left off once the room cools down. <LINE> <LINE> When the barrel is empty (tap empty, no batch, slots empty) it can be picked up or dismantled; moving it keeps the fitted parts, dismantling it loses them.
%1 - not in your inventory (a part on the ground or in a container cannot be fitted)
This cellar was built to an older layout: its slot holds %1 bottles and the Bottle Rack does nothing here. Tear the cellar down and build it again for the rack to work.
Old cellar: the rack has no effect
Every resting job in this cellar
The bottle slot grows from %1 to %2 bottles
Wait for the running job to finish
Take the bottle count down to %2 first: now %1 / %2

A still distils. The fermented liquid in the bucket is heated over charcoal, condenses and runs down into the tap; ten litres of wine leave three litres of spirit behind. <LINE> <LINE> Pick a recipe, then press Prepare: it fetches the bucket, the fuel and the additive out of your inventory. Hover any line on the card to see where that ingredient comes from. If the button stays dim, the line under it names what is short. <LINE> <LINE> The fuel slot takes twelve charcoal and every run burns six. Fill it to the top and you can leave the fire alone for two batches. <LINE> <LINE> The finished spirit sits in the tap until you draw it into a container; the next batch waits on that. <LINE> <LINE> The upgrades on the second tab shorten the run or raise the yield, and their slots open at Brewing 3, 6 and 9. From Brewing 9 on, every run gives three and a half litres instead of three. <LINE> <LINE> A still heats itself, so the weather changes nothing here - the strip at the top says the temperature is not checked. Watch the charcoal instead.
A second click cancels the batch.

The cellar is where bottles wait. Nothing is brewed here; a full bottle left in the rack simply ages on its own. <LINE> <LINE> Every row in the list is one group: the container and what is in it, how many bottles, how much time has passed and how much is left, and the state. Hover a row to read the two numbers apart. When the time is up the bottle turns into its aged form by itself - wine rests in a week, raw spirit becomes cognac in two. <LINE> <LINE> To take bottles out, select a row first and then use one of the buttons below: either the whole group or a single bottle from it. The third button needs no selection, it collects everything that has finished resting. The fourth button needs no selection either: it places every full bottle on you or nearby (on the floor or in containers close by) that can go in the cellar. The slot holds 50 bottles. <LINE> <LINE> The counter only runs while the cellar is cool. If the strip at the top reads 0-15 °C you are fine; a cellar that warms up or freezes stops the clock, harms nothing, and carries on once the temperature comes back. <LINE> <LINE> The second tab holds the upgrades. A part fitted here shortens the resting time, widens the temperature the cellar puts up with, or (the Bottle Rack) raises the slot to 100 bottles; the slots open at Brewing 3, 6 and 9. <LINE> <LINE> Put several bottles of the same drink in together - they collapse into one row in the list, and a single click takes them all back out.
The cellar is empty - put a bottle in the slot to age it.
Select a row, then take it with the buttons below. Take all aged and Place all work without a selection.
The cellar is too warm - the timer stopped
The cellar is too cold - the timer stopped
The cellar is cool - resting is under way
Cannot be moved or dismantled while a batch is running.
Fully aged but not converted - take the bottle out of the slot and put it back
Your carrying limit lets at most %1 bottles go this click; press again once they are placed.
No full bottles on you or nearby that can go in the cellar
%1 suitable bottles, but the slot only has room for %2; the rest stay with you.

Skill at pressing must, fermenting and bottling. Higher levels unlock new recipes and the wine you bottle comes out at a better grade. <LINE> Bottling and salvaging also require the Distiller's Notebook to have been read; the skill alone is not enough.

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 1 - Bottling <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Draw a fermented batch into a container and get Table Wine. <LINE> You can ferment apple must and bottle Cider. <LINE> Requires the Distiller's Notebook; the skill alone is not enough. <INDENT:0>
<RGB:1,1,0>Level 10 - Master's hand <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Barrel and still batches you start take a further 15%% less time. <LINE> Barrel 36.7 h, still 6.8 h. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 2 - Salvage and beer <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Turn a spoiled liquid into vinegar with fruit and sugar. <LINE> Bottle the raw beer from the barrel into Table Beer. <LINE> Bottling opens for vermouth, sherry and port. <LINE> All of them require the Distiller's Notebook. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 3 - Select grade <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> The wine you bottle comes out as Select Wine and the beer as Select Beer: more calories, better morale, a little stronger. <LINE> Bottling unlocks for raki, vodka, raw spirit, whiskey, rum, gin and tequila. <LINE> The first upgrade slot on your stations opens. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 4 - Faster fermentation <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Barrel batches you start take 10%% less time: 43.2 h instead of 48 h. <LINE> You can bottle mead. <LINE> You can bottle champagne. <LINE> You can build a Bottle Rack for the cellar. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 5 - Select grade for spirits <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> The raki you bottle comes out as Select Raki. <LINE> Vodka, whiskey, rum, cider, vermouth, sherry, port, champagne, curaçao, gin, coffee liqueur and tequila have no grades; their quality is born in the cellar. <LINE> The mead you bottle comes out as Mead (Select). <LINE> You can bottle liqueur, curaçao and coffee liqueur. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 6 - Temperature tolerance <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> A barrel batch you start keeps working 2 °C colder and 2 °C hotter. <LINE> The window becomes 10-32 °C instead of 12-30 °C. <LINE> The second upgrade slot on your stations opens. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 7 - Master's work <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> The wine you bottle comes out as Master's Wine and the beer as Master's Beer. <LINE> The best grade the fermenting branch can reach. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Level 8 - Master's work in spirits <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> The raki you bottle comes out as Master's Raki. <LINE> The mead you bottle comes out as Mead (Master's). <LINE> The best grade the distilling branch can reach. <INDENT:0>
<RGB:1,1,0>Level 9 - Still yield <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> A still batch you start gives 3.5 litres instead of 3. <LINE> The third upgrade slot on your stations opens. <INDENT:0>

Şıra ezme, mayalanma ve şişeleme becerisi. Seviye yükseldikçe yeni tarifler açılır ve şişelediğin şarap daha iyi bir kademeden çıkar. <LINE> Şişeleme ve kurtarma tarifleri ayrıca Çilingir Defteri'ni okumuş olmayı ister; beceri tek başına yetmez.

<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 1 - Şişeleme <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Mayalanmış partiyi kaba çekip Şarap (Sofralık) elde edersin. <LINE> Elma şırasını mayalandırıp Elma Şarabı şişeleyebilirsin. <LINE> Çilingir Defteri şart; beceri tek başına yetmez. <INDENT:0>
<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 10 - Usta eli <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Senin başlattığın fıçı ve imbik partilerinin süresi ayrıca %%15 kısalır. <LINE> Fıçı 36,7 sa, imbik 6,8 sa. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 2 - Kurtarma ve bira <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Bozulmuş bir sıvıyı meyve ve şekerle sirkeye çevirirsin. <LINE> Fıçıdaki ham birayı şişeleyip Bira (Sofralık) elde edersin. <LINE> Şişeleme kapısı üçe daha açılır: Vermut Şişele, Şeri Şişele, Port Şarabı Şişele. <LINE> Hepsi Çilingir Defteri ister. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 3 - Seçme kademe <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Şişelediğin şarap Şarap (Seçme), bira Bira (Seçme) olur: daha çok kalori, daha çok moral, biraz daha sert. <LINE> Şişeleme kapısı yediye çıkar: Rakı Şişele, Votka Şişele, Suma Şişele, Viski Şişele, Rom Şişele, Cin Şişele, Tekila Şişele. <LINE> İstasyonların birinci geliştirme yuvası açılır. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 4 - Hızlı mayalanma <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Senin başlattığın fıçı partileri %%10 daha kısa sürer: 48 sa yerine 43,2 sa. <LINE> Bal şarabı şişeleyebilirsin. <LINE> Şampanya şişeleyebilirsin. <LINE> Mahzen için Şişe Rafı yapabilirsin. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 5 - Damıtıkta seçme kademe <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Şişelediğin rakı Rakı (Seçme) olur. <LINE> Votka, viski, rom, elma şarabı, vermut, şeri, port şarabı, şampanya, curaçao, cin, kahve likörü ve tekila kademesizdir; kaliteleri mahzende doğar. <LINE> Şişelediğin bal şarabı Bal Şarabı (Seçme) olur. <LINE> Likör, curaçao ve kahve likörü şişeleyebilirsin. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 6 - Sıcaklık toleransı <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Senin başlattığın fıçı partisi 2 °C daha soğukta ve 2 °C daha sıcakta da işler. <LINE> Pencere 12-30 °C yerine 10-32 °C olur. <LINE> İstasyonların ikinci geliştirme yuvası açılır. <INDENT:0>
<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 7 - Usta işi <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Şişelediğin şarap Şarap (Usta İşi), bira Bira (Usta İşi) olur. <LINE> Mayalanma kolunun en iyi kademesi. <INDENT:0>

<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 8 - Damıtıkta usta işi <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Şişelediğin rakı Rakı (Usta İşi) olur. <LINE> Şişelediğin bal şarabı Bal Şarabı (Usta İşi) olur. <LINE> Damıtma kolunun en iyi kademesi. <INDENT:0>
<RGB:1,1,0>Seviye 9 - İmbik verimi <LINE> <RGB:1,1,1> <INDENT:10> Senin başlattığın imbik partisi 3 litre yerine 3,5 litre verir. <LINE> İstasyonların üçüncü geliştirme yuvası açılır. <INDENT:0>
Brewing I: "An Introduction to Home Winemaking"
Brewing II: "The Secret of the Yeast"
Brewing IV: "The Taste of the Glass"
Brewing V: "Master of the Distiller's Table"
Adds a '[CTB] Debug' entry to the stations' right-click menu. Only admins or a game started with -debug see it.
How often all six notebooks spawn: the five themed volumes (wine, grain, distilling, cordials, parts) and the full notebook that teaches every branch. Bottling recipes are learned from them.
Multiplies the growth time of the mod's ten plants. 2 is twice as slow. Vanilla crops are unaffected.
How strong the station upgrade parts are.
Below this the cellar stops aging; bottles do not spoil.
Above this the cellar stops aging; bottles do not spoil.
Below this the barrel waits; the batch does not spoil.
Above this the barrel waits; the batch does not spoil.
Multiplies barrel, still and cellar times. 0.5 is twice as fast, 2 twice as slow.
How fast the Brewing skill levels up.

A thick, fleshy agave leaf with spined edges; in Turkish it goes by 'sabir otu', the patience herb. Under the press it gives a syrup as sweet as honey, and the tequila chain begins there.
Not foraged but sown, and it stands in the field for years.

Twelve agave, a bucket and a stirring utensil at the hand press: the bucket fills to the brim with agave juice. <LINE> Only appears at the press. <LINE> Agave juice is a syrup as sweet as honey; its real purpose is the barrel.

A handful of anise seed. The one thing that turns raw spirit into raki.
Found in kitchen cupboards and on grocery shelves, foraged from the wild, or grown in the field from seed.

A handful of blue-purple juniper berries. The first choice for gin; rosemary or sage give the same raw gin.
Foraged in the woods among the scrub, plentiful in autumn, or grown in the field from seed.
Draws one litre of malt wort from the bucket into an empty container. <LINE> Barley water is unfermented: a sweet, filling, alcohol-free malt drink.

Draws a third of a litre of malt wort into an empty beer bottle or can. <LINE> Barley water is unfermented: sweet, filling and alcohol-free. <LINE> A ten-litre bucket makes thirty-three small bottles; they cannot go in the cellar.

Draws one litre of raw mead from the bucket into an empty container. <LINE> Brewing sets the grade: 4 table, 5-7 select, 8-10 master's. <LINE> A ten-litre batch makes ten bottles; seven in-game days in the cellar age one.

Boils five jars of honey in a bucket of ten litres of clean water: the same bucket comes back with ten litres of honey must. <LINE> No mechanical fire required. <LINE> The must is non-alcoholic; with yeast in the barrel it becomes mead.

A copper elbow curved like a swan's neck.
Fits the still and the cellar, cutting the time on the raki branch - resting included. Not for a barrel.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
Hammers five pieces of copper scrap and a small sheet of metal into the curve of a swan's neck. <LINE> Fits the still and the cellar, and cuts the time on the raki branch - resting included.
Draws one litre of raw beer from the bucket into an empty container. <LINE> Brewing sets the grade: 2 table, 3-6 select, 7-10 master's. <LINE> A ten-litre batch makes ten bottles.

Draws a third of a litre of raw beer into an empty beer bottle or can. <LINE> The grade band matches the one-litre bottle: 2 table, 3-6 select, 7-10 master's. <LINE> A ten-litre batch makes thirty-three small bottles; they cannot go in the cellar.
Draws one litre of barrel-fermented boza into an empty container. <LINE> Boza has no grades. It is barely alcoholic but the most filling drink in the pack.

Draws a third of a litre of boza into an empty beer bottle or can. <LINE> Boza has no grades; only the volume is one third. <LINE> A ten-litre batch makes thirty-three small bottles; they cannot go in the cellar.

Turns two litres of tainted water into vinegar with fruit and sugar; the container is used up. <LINE> A failed ferment leaves no tainted water in the barrel - and no must either, since the inputs are spent the moment it starts.
Everything a distiller learned in a lifetime went into this notebook; he never gave the secret away, he just left the recipe. It does the work of four volumes, so it is rarely found.

Draws one litre of raw gin into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full one takes its place. <LINE> No grades; the grade is born in the cellar: it ages in fourteen in-game days. <LINE> A three-litre distilling makes three bottles.

Draws one litre of raw curaçao into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full one takes its place. <LINE> No grades; the grade is born in the cellar: it ages in fourteen in-game days. <LINE> A three-litre steeping makes three bottles.

The cover is blackened with soot; it was written beside the still.
Teaches the bottling of moonshine, raki, vodka, whiskey, rum, tequila and gin.

A coppersmith's notebook, full of drawings.
Teaches how to build all twelve station parts, from the coil to the bottle rack.

Its pages are stained with must and foam, every step from the harvest to the bottle.
Teaches bottling wine, cider and champagne, the beer branch and salvaging a spoiled batch.

A sweet little book filled in a careful hand.
Teaches the branch running from mead to the liqueurs and grenadine.
A fleshy rosette plant. Perennial, cold hardy.
A herb crop. Annual, killed by winter.
A dwarf juniper bush. Perennial, cold hardy.
A dwarf pear bush. Perennial, cold hardy.
A thorny blackberry bush. Perennial, cold hardy.
A dwarf apple bush. Perennial, cold hardy.
A dwarf peach bush. Perennial, cold hardy.
A low grape vine. Perennial, cold hardy.
A dwarf cherry bush. Perennial, cold hardy.
A dense blueberry bush. Perennial, cold hardy.

Twenty apples, a bucket and a stirring utensil at the hand press: the bucket fills to the brim with apple must. <LINE> This must is separate from grape must; cider comes only from it. Apples also go into Press Fruit. <LINE> Only appears at the press.

Draws one litre of raw cider into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full cider bottle takes its place. <LINE> Cider has no grades; the grade is born in the cellar: it ages in seven in-game days.

Crushes four pomegranates with two units of sugar into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full one takes its place. <LINE> No alcohol: no cellar, no resting, no grades. <LINE> Cherries will do instead; four fruit make one bottle.

A distilling pot with a copper worm.
It heats itself: every run burns six charcoal.
Most recipes take ten litres in and give three; gin takes three, gives three. Picked up or dismantled only when empty; dismantling loses fitted parts.

A bent copper pipe through a cork: gas out, no air in.
Raises the yield on every recipe of the wine branch. Not for a cellar, where there is no yield in litres.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.

A cork, two pieces of copper scrap and a ripped sheet: a small lock that lets the gas out and no air in. No hammer needed. <LINE> Raises the yield on every recipe of the wine branch; it does not fit a cellar.

Draws a litre of raw coffee liqueur into a glass bottle. <LINE> No grades; it ages in the cellar in fourteen in-game days. <LINE> Three litres make three bottles; it also wants a full bottle of raw spirit - no clay jars, the bottle comes back empty.
Draws one litre of raw liqueur from the bucket into an empty container. <LINE> Cherry liqueur has no grades and does not rest in the cellar. <LINE> A three-litre batch makes three bottles.

A rack where bottles rest.
Time only runs in the cellar; taking a bottle out pauses it. Keep it COOL or resting stops.
Holds 50 bottles, 100 with a Bottle Rack. Picked up or dismantled only when empty; dismantling loses fitted parts.

Grain that has been sprouted and dried; this is where both beer and boza begin.
Not eaten on its own: it goes into boiling water and becomes wort.

Sprouts and dries 1-20 dried grain sheaves or seeds on the Large Plant Drying Rack: two in-game days later you get exactly as many malt. <LINE> Barley, wheat and rye all work; fresh sheaves must be dried first. <LINE> Only appears at the rack.

Sugared fruit in an empty glass jar, cloth over the mouth, and the wild yeast in the air does the rest. One unit of sugar goes in (a bag holds 30). <LINE> Two in-game days on the Small Plant Drying Rack make it a yeast culture. <LINE> The jar stays with the culture; once the culture is used in the barrel or dried, the jar comes back empty.

Cloth over the mouth, sugared fruit inside, and the wild yeast in the air doing the work. Do not shake it, stir it or open it to look.
Put it on the Small Plant Drying Rack and let two in-game days pass. A cold rack means yeast that never settles.

A mature, bubbling, living starter; this is what turns sugar into alcohol.
Its place is the barrel: must or mash, no batch starts without it. Once the culture is used, its glass jar comes back empty.

Dries and crumbles a mature yeast culture into baking yeast, and the empty jar comes back. <LINE> The yeast has ten uses: bread, cake, baguette and pizza dough each take one. <LINE> The barrel still wants cultures; this way out is optional.

Put the cloth-covered jar on the Small Plant Drying Rack and wait two in-game days: each jar becomes one yeast culture, up to 20 at a time. <LINE> Only appears at the rack. <LINE> Yeast will not settle in the cold; keep the rack warm.

A wooden barrel where must and mash ferment; it holds 50 litres and runs one batch. Ambient temperature matters: outside 12-30 C fermenting takes longer.
Picked up or dismantled only when empty; dismantling loses fitted parts.

A large wooden barrel where must and mash ferment; it holds 100 litres and runs three batches at once. Ambient temperature matters: outside 12-30 C fermenting takes longer.
Picked up or dismantled only when empty; dismantling loses fitted parts.

A heavy straining cloth of sheet and denim; it squeezes the mash dry.
Fits the barrel and the still, and raises the yield on the potato branch. Not for a cellar.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
Sews a sheet and two denim strips into layers and binds them with twine; no hammer needed. <LINE> Fits the barrel and the still, and raises the yield on the potato branch.

A long paddle of hammered copper; it keeps the boiling mash off the bottom.
Fits the barrel and cuts the time on the beer branch. Not for a still or a cellar.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
Hammers four pieces of copper scrap onto the end of a plank: a long-handled paddle. <LINE> Fits the barrel and cuts the time on the beer branch.

A coarse rasp of punched sheet metal; it turns the mash into pulp.
Fits the barrel and the still, and cuts the time on the potato branch. It does not fit a cellar.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
Punches teeth into two small sheets of metal and nails them onto a plank: a coarse rasp. <LINE> Fits the barrel and the still, and cuts the time on the potato branch.

A hoop carved from oak; it hurries the talk between wine and wood.
Cuts the time on most recipes of the wine branch, resting included; other branches gain nothing.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
Hoops four planks together with six nails into an oak band. <LINE> Cuts the time on most recipes of the wine branch, resting included.

Twenty fruit, a bucket and a stirring utensil at the hand press: the bucket fills to the brim with must. <LINE> Only appears at the press. <LINE> Must is non-alcoholic; its real purpose is the barrel.

Boils fifteen corn in a bucket of ten litres of clean water: the same bucket comes back with ten litres of malt wort. <LINE> It is the same fluid Boil Malt Wort makes; corn is an alternative raw material for whiskey, not a separate product.

Twenty potatoes, a bucket and a stirring utensil at the hand press: the bucket fills to the brim with potato mash. <LINE> Only appears at the press. <LINE> The mash is a raw starch slurry; its real purpose is the barrel.

Draws one litre of raw port into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full port bottle takes its place. <LINE> Its input is unfermented must. <LINE> No grades; the grade is born in the cellar: it ages in twenty-one in-game days.

Draws one litre of raw spirit from the bucket into an empty container; a handful of anise is used up as well. <LINE> Brewing sets the grade: 3-4 table, 5-7 select, 8-10 master's. <LINE> A three-litre still run makes three bottles.

Draws one litre of raw rum into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full one takes its place. <LINE> No grades; the grade is born in the cellar: it ages in fourteen in-game days. <LINE> A three-litre still run makes three bottles.

Draws one litre of raw sparkling wine into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full one takes its place. <LINE> No grades; the grade is born in the cellar: it ages in fourteen in-game days. <LINE> Ageing changes the name, not the icon.
Draws one litre of raw wine from the bucket into an empty container. <LINE> Brewing sets the grade: 1-2 table, 3-6 select, 7-10 master's wine. <LINE> A ten-litre batch makes ten bottles.

Runs cooked sugar beet pulp through a strainer or cheese cloth; a thick syrup stays in the pot and the strainer is not used up. <LINE> It will not open while the pulp is uncooked. <LINE> Make Sugar turns the syrup into a bag right away; no waiting.

Mashes five sugar beets in a pot holding 1.5 litres of water; the pot fills with pulp. <LINE> Cook the pulp on a stove (two in-game hours), then take it to Strain Sugar Beet Pulp. <LINE> Five beets make one bag of sugar (30 units).

Fifteen units of sugar go into a bucket of ten litres of clean water (a bag holds 30): it comes back with ten litres of sugar must, which becomes rum mash in the barrel. <LINE> Sugar, brown sugar, cubes and packets all work.

Dries a pot of sugar beet syrup into one bag of sugar (30 units); the pot counts as whole and comes back empty. <LINE> Syrup that turned into sugar-beet sugar on its own works too. <LINE> Recipes that want sugar will not take the pot; make a bag.

A sack sewn from ripped sheets; it keeps the spent hops out of the barrel.
Fits the barrel and raises the yield on the beer branch. Not for a still or a cellar.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
Turns four ripped sheets into a sack with twine and fills it with dried hops; no hammer needed. <LINE> Fits the barrel and raises the yield on the beer branch.

Draws one litre of raw sherry into an empty glass bottle; the bottle is used up and a full sherry bottle takes its place. <LINE> Its input is fully fermented wine. <LINE> No grades; the grade is born in the cellar: it ages in twenty-one in-game days.

A copper pipe hammered into coil after coil; the distiller's one way to steal time.
Fits the barrel, the still and the cellar, and cuts the time - resting included.
Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
Hammers six pieces of copper scrap and a small sheet of metal into a coiled worm. <LINE> Fits the barrel, the still and the cellar, and cuts the time - resting included.
Sours one litre of raw wine in a cloth-covered container; the container is used up. <LINE> The vinegar is used in cooking recipes.

A rack with a hole for each bottle.
Fits the cellar only and grows the bottle slot from 50 to 100 bottles.
It cannot come off while the slot holds over 50. Tear down or dismantle a station without removing its parts and they are lost.
